name: Farren's Report
summary: In Southshore, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's report carries his findings on the local naga. He hopes the dispatch will win him a return to Stormwind.

sections.title: A Ticket Out of Southshore
sections.body:
Lieutenant Farren Orinelle grew weary of Southshore's embattled coast, its leaders, and its remote frontier. He sent adventurers to hunt the Daggerspine naga and gather proof of their threat. Then he shaped their findings into a formal report.

Farren plans to send the dispatch to Major Samuelson, captain of the guard in Stormwind Keep, instead of his commander, Marshal Redpath. Samuelson trained Farren, and Farren hopes the report will prove his competence and earn him an immediate transfer to Stormwind City's comforts.

faq.answer: Farren's Report records Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's operations against the Daggerspine naga threatening Southshore's beaches.

faq.q: Why does Farren want this delivered to Stormwind?
faq.answer: Farren hopes to leave Southshore and return to Stormwind City. He sends the report to Major Samuelson, his former mentor and captain of the Stormwind guard, in hope of a favorable transfer.

faq.q: Why is Farren keeping the report a secret from Redpath?
faq.answer: Farren wants to avoid scrutiny from Marshal Redpath and Southshore's leaders. They might resent an officer using a local threat to arrange a personal transfer to safety in the capital.

faq.q: How does Major Samuelson react upon receiving it?
faq.answer: Major Samuelson praises his former student for taking initiative against the Southshore naga. He promises to consider the report while reviewing guard assignments in the coming month.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Farren's Report reveals maneuvering within its military, as officers in distant Hillsbrad seek safer duty in Stormwind.
As a human of the Alliance, carrying Farren's Report connects besieged Southshore with the royal court in Stormwind Keep.
